summary: M3-S01 (two Case ValidationRules — Priority_Required_On_Agent_Save, Origin_Must_Be_Known — with the Bypass_Case_Intake_Validation clause) passed all 3 runnable declared acceptance tests plus both always-on structural checks: xml (3/3 parse: package.xml plus both validationRule-meta.xml files), manifest (ValidationRule:Case two-way consistent, both members explicit, no wildcard, both files present), and the declared checker skills/admin/validation-rules/scripts/check_validation_rules.py --manifest-dir artefacts/M3-S01 --strict (exit 0, score 100, 0 findings). check-outputs: ok, no missing/empty/malformed. 1 manual test (W01: bypass clause, blank-guard shape, component-field-only, message quality) deferred to the M3 gate — Given/When/Then shape present with named observable outcomes, so usable, not ticked here. Grep-confirmed directly from disk: both formulas open with NOT($Permission.Bypass_Case_Intake_Validation); both use ISBLANK(TEXT(<picklist>)) as the blank test (Origin_Must_Be_Known uses ISPICKVAL only to enumerate the three valid values, never as the blank test); the referenced custom permission exists at artefacts/M2-S01/customPermissions/Bypass_Case_Intake_Validation.customPermission-meta.xml; both errorMessage values are 218 characters (under the 255 cap); both rules are active=true; neither formula names a compound address field. Status set to tested.
confidence_rationale: Step 7 rubric, HIGH row: every declared test either ran or was correctly classified as manual, both always-on checks completed, and every result came from an exit code this agent observed. No MEDIUM trigger fired — no command test was refused, no coverage-gap exclusion was needed (ValidationRule has a standalone source file per devops/metadata-api-coverage-gaps), and check-outputs reported no missing, empty or malformed declared output. No LOW trigger fired — the one declared checker existed and ran, the artefact directory holds 4 files (3 XML, 2 markdown, one of which — validation-bypass-note.md — is a declared output rather than metadata), and every exit code was captured to tests/M3-S01/.

process_observations.observation: The step's own documented fixture claim held on re-run: check_validation_rules.py --strict against these exact two rules printed 'Scanned 2 validation rule(s) across 2 file(s); 0 finding(s) detected.' and exited 0. The REVIEW rule the plan's inputs.note warns about ('picklist logic has no explicit blank guard', fired by ISPICKVAL( with no ISBLANK() in the same formula) does not fire here because both formulas gate the blank case with ISBLANK(TEXT(...)) before any ISPICKVAL comparison runs.

The bypass-guard REVIEW rule in the checker (fires when an active rule's formula contains no $PERMISSION. token) also does not fire: both formulas open with NOT($Permission.Bypass_Case_Intake_Validation), and the permission it names exists as a real CustomPermission artefact from a dependency step rather than a forward reference to nothing.

acceptance_tests[0].description in plan.json claims the declared checker verifies 'every field token in every formula resolves' and 'an errorDisplayField that resolves'. Reading check_validation_rules.py end to end (audit_rule, collect_rules, main) shows no field inventory, no describe call and no cross-check against any object/field metadata anywhere in the script — it only inspects the formula string and error-message text. The step's own deploy-order.md already names this gap under 'Marked as ungrounded' item 6; this run independently confirms it by reading the checker source rather than taking the note's word for it. Priority, Origin and the $Permission name were still verified by this run against M1-S01, M1-S02 and M2-S01's artefacts directly (see the manual-test table), so the fields do resolve — the exit code just does not carry that proof.

deploy-order.md item 5 (A12) records that these two rules are correct but not proven to be invariants: if any automation re-saves Priority or Origin after the initial insert, a custom validation rule does not re-fire on a workflow field update, so a later automation write could leave a Case in a state the rule would have blocked at insert. The note assumes M4-S03's before-save flow is the only future writer of these two fields, but M4-S03 is not yet built at this point in the milestone sequence, so the assumption is unresolved rather than false.
M3-S01 is now tested but its documentation (workbook rows, traceability entries, decisions log) has not yet been updated to reflect this test run.
process_observations.followup_reason: Because the doc keeper is the agent that carries a tested step's evidence into PLAN.md, the workbook and traceability.md, and this run performed no documentation writes.
